Subject: Mutual success beacons & exit sentinels — MAP + acceptance tests

Sam / Julio — attaching our initial MAP draft plus a concise acceptance-scenarios doc. Goal for this thread: lock the objective success beacons (what you call success), the exit sentinels (hard thresholds that trigger rollback/no-go), and a minimal acceptance test suite we can run during the 4-week evaluation.

Key asks from ClearMap: please confirm the top-3 success metrics you care about and flag any regulatory/test constraints (data retention, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts) we must include in the acceptance run.

High-level we propose:
- Success beacons: 1) 95th percentile inference latency <= 200ms for 512-token average prompts; 2) end-to-end cost/unit <= $0.004 per generated token at steady-state using suggested batching; 3) >= 98% safety/label concordance on your 2k sample prompt set.
- Exit sentinels (hard stop): sustained latency > 500ms for 5 consecutive sampling windows (5m each); safety regression > 5% against baseline set; any confirmed data leakage or PII retention beyond agreed TTL.
- Acceptance tests: smoke (latency + correctness on 200 prompts), stability (24h load test at expected QPS), conformance (10 security checklist items + evidence bundle).

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (owners/dates), acceptance-scenarios.md (test list).

Proposed next steps:
1) You review and mark primary success beacons by Thu 12/3.
2) We finalize MAP owners and schedule the first smoke run week of 12/7.
3) Signoff on acceptance-scenarios to unlock Dedicated trial.

Evelyn

Subject: Re: Mutual success beacons & exit sentinels — MAP + acceptance tests

Evelyn — thanks for the clear framing and the MAP. Quick responses from our side:

1) Top success metrics (priority):
   - Primary: 95th pct latency for typical clinical prompts <= 250ms (we can tolerate 200ms but want to budget to 250ms as realistic).
   - Secondary: Reduction in human-review workload by >= 30% on triaged notes (we'll provide baseline numbers).
   - Tertiary: No safety-related false positives that materially block workflows (>99% operational pass on high-risk prompts).

2) Exit sentinels — agree with the spirit but request the latency threshold be 700ms for hard stop (our ops team is conservative). Also: add an explicit data handling sentinel — any attempt to surface PHI in logs/evidence must be treated as immediate mitigation + investigation.

3) We will review the MAP spreadsheet and acceptance-scenarios doc and get detailed feedback by Friday 12/4. Can you also include a short SLA note for the Dedicated trial (expected uptime and support response targets)?

Thanks — Sam

Subject: Re: Mutual success beacons & exit sentinels — MAP + acceptance tests

Sam — appreciate the clarifications. Noted on the latency guard (700ms hard stop). I've sketched an operational tolerance ladder in the MAP (see MAP-draft-v1.xlsx tab: Sentinels) so we have staged responses:

- Alert (yellow): 95p > 300ms for 15m window -> ops notification, reduce batch sizes, enable burst to Dedicated pool.
- Mitigate (orange): 95p > 450ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> circuit to lower-cost model variant + escalate to support.
- Stop (red): sustained > 700ms for 5 consecutive 5m windows -> pause trial traffic and initiate post-mortem.

On acceptance-scenarios.md — added two items:
- Conformance evidence: SOC2 checklist items we will provide and where ClearMap needs to corroborate configs.
- Data retention test: end-to-end TTL enforcement test + audit log extraction for a 30-day window.

I'll attach a small matrix (latency-cost-matrix.csv) with the rough projected per-token unit economics for different batching and quantization knobs; that should help align on the cost beacon.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual success beacons & exit sentinels — MAP + acceptance tests

Adding a couple of acceptance test specifics from product/QA side so we can hand them to your test engineers:

1) Smoke test (owner: ClearMap / co-owned) — 200 clinical prompts (mixed-length): verify response shape, token-count estimate, and sample latency distribution. Pass if no more than 3 prompts exceed the 95th percentile latency threshold.
2) Stability test (owner: Redwood) — 24h at expected pilot QPS with periodic burst to 3x for 10 minutes every 4 hours. Monitor KV-cache hit rate and tail latencies; fail if tail latency spikes >2x baseline more than twice.
3) Concordance test (owner: ClearMap) — run your human-review comparison: provide 500 labeled prompts, we'll return model results and you measure human-review reduction.
4) Security checklist (owner: ClearMap + Redwood) — run data-handling smoke: ingest a 50-record test file tagged with synthetic PHI and verify TTL deletion and no PHI appears in any debug traces or logs.

I'll add these as discrete test cases into the MAP sheet with pass/fail criteria and owners. If everyone agrees, we aim to run smoke on 2026-12-08 and the longer stability run on 2026-12-09/10.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summary and actions (agreed):

1) Success beacons (finalized):
   - Latency beacon: 95th pct clinical prompts <= 250ms (ClearMap prioritized, but Redwood will aim for 200ms operationally; sentinel ladder documented).
   - Human-review reduction >= 30% on the provided baseline sample.
   - Safety/concordance: >= 98% on the flagged high-risk set.

2) Exit sentinels (finalized):
   - Operational stop: sustained 95p > 700ms for 5 consecutive 5m windows.
   - Safety stop: confirmed PHI leakage or safety regression > 5% -> immediate pause + investigation.

3) Acceptance tests + schedule:
   - Smoke (200 prompts) — run 2026-12-08 (owners: ClearMap + Redwood).
   - Stability (24h) — run 2026-12-09/10 (owner: Redwood).
   - Concordance (500 labeled) — begin 2026-12-07; results shared by 2026-12-14 (owner: ClearMap).
   - Data handling smoke (synthetic PHI) — part of smoke run; evidence artifact to be uploaded to Drive.

4) Documentation & evidence: Marissa to publish latency-cost-matrix.csv and updated MAP (tab: TestCases + Sentinels). Karthik to push test-case rows into the MAP sheet. Sam to confirm acceptance metrics by 2026-12-04 (noted earlier) — if delayed, we'll default to the beacons above.

5) SLA note: Ben to circulate a short trial SLA (uptime, priority support RTO) by EOD 12/8.

If that matches your understanding, please reply-all with any redlines. Once Sam confirms, we'll lock the MAP and schedule the smoke run.

Best — Evelyn
